conviction_note: A near non-result. This is a regulated FTSE 100 water utility with 13 analysts covering it. Q1 trading was pre-released in July, and the regulatory events that matter (the Ofwat wastewater probe, the EPA rating, the cost-change draft, the CFO exit) are all public and visible on the tape. The peer read-through from United Utilities on 12 Nov is already in SVT's price. The one live new line is a likely upgrade to the FY27 performance-incentive (ODI) guide. Last year the interim ODI raise was sold (-1.1%), but the FY26 EPS-outlook upgrade was bought (+2.3%). Against that, the stock sits at a 1-year high (3,350p on 13 Nov), above the April broker targets, with shorts adding 0.2pp. So p_up is 52 and the move is sized on the name's own guidance-event reactions, lifted for the stage's measured understatement (2.5%). impact_sum (+0.1) and impact_scaled (+0.1) agree.

already_public.what: Q1 FY27 trading update: performance in line with expectations; confident of at least £50m total performance incentives (ODIs+PCDs) in FY27; ~£440m capex in Q1 (+22% y/y); on track for £2.2-2.5bn FY27 capex; core bank facilities refinanced to £1.65bn; interims dated 18 Nov 2026

FY26 results: 2028 adjusted EPS outlook upgraded to at least 250p (from 224p); FY27 capex £2.2-2.5bn, RCV growth 13% to £17.4bn; FY27 ODI target at least £50m; over £300m ODIs to 2030 reaffirmed; dividend policy of at least CPIH growth
Ofwat concludes its wastewater investigation with no financial penalty (undertakings instead)
Ofwat 2026 Cost Change draft: £329m allowed against £481m requested; final decision due by mid-December 2026
CFO Helen Miles to step down (to Vistry) on a 12-month notice period; search under way
EA Environmental Performance Assessment for 2025: Severn Trent the only 4-star company, its seventh consecutive year

new_in_release.expect: FY27 ODI guidance (at least £50m) likely raised: SVT has raised it at every H1/FY across AMP8 so far (HY26 from at least £25m to at least £40m; FY26 came in ahead). Mild positive, though last year's raise was sold. The 2028 EPS outlook (at least 250p) is probably reiterated, with an upside tail from the reopener.
H1 underlying PBIT/EPS not pre-released. Allowed-revenue growth should drive it, as at United Utilities (+7% underlying operating profit). Direction against consensus: unknown.
Interim mechanically about +3.5% (CPIH policy; UU +3.5%). No information.
Cost-change response and a possible CFO successor. Commentary on the strengthened Water Bill. Mostly neutral.
Net debt and gearing rising with capex (63.6% at FY26). An equity-need question is possible but unknown.

findings.finding: A likely raise to the FY27 performance-incentive guide. SVT has lifted its ODI guide at each interim and final in AMP8, it kept the EA's only 4-star EPA rating for 2025 (published end-Oct 2026), and Ofwat closed its wastewater probe with no fine. The release probably raises the 'at least £50m' FY27 ODI guide, the one guidance line likely to move.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HY26 interim (19 Nov 2025) raised the FY26 ODI guide from at least £25m to at least £40m: stock -1.10%. FY26 results (20 May 2026) upgraded the 2028 EPS outlook: +2.26%. Mixed, so the sign is weak.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. A habitual ODI beat is the sell-side base case on a 13-analyst name, and the stock at a 1-year high reflects it. Only the size of the raise is unknown. If the market expected a large raise, the stock would have outrun UU into the print; it has moved in line (both near highs, both -1.5 to -1.7% on 17 Nov).

findings.finding: Ofwat's 2026 Cost Change draft allowed SVT £329m of the £481m requested (68%). The final decision is due in December, so the interim will carry only the company's response and any change to the reopener assumptions behind the 2028 EPS outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No SVT-specific reaction to the 13 Aug draft could be isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for three months, so largely priced. Only an explicit statement that the haircut trims the outlook would be new, and that is not the base case given the 'at least' framing.

lessons_applied: abs_move_pct raised from 2.0 to 2.5: 'the move is in the guide' plus 'too small by a factor of three'. A likely ODI-guide change makes this a guidance event, though the name's own maxima (3.74%) and 14% realised vol keep it far below the stage's 9% guidance-change base.
Findings and p_up unchanged: the ODI-raise finding was already sized with last year's sold raise in mind, and the pre-released Q1 had no reported_quarter finding resting on it.
